title: Properties of Materials
description: Objects are made of different materials. Materials have properties like hard, soft, rough, smooth, shiny, and dull.

exercises.question: Which word describes how something FEELS when you touch it?
exercises.exp: Texture describes how something feels — rough, smooth, bumpy, or soft.

exercises.question: A wooden block is HARD. What is the opposite of hard?
exercises.exp: Soft is the opposite of hard. A pillow is soft.

exercises.question: Which material would you choose to make a raincoat?
exercises.exp: Waterproof plastic keeps water out — perfect for a raincoat!

exercises.question: A mirror is SHINY. Which object is also shiny?
exercises.exp: A polished spoon reflects light and looks shiny.

exercises.question: What property tells us how HEAVY something is?
exercises.exp: Mass tells us how heavy an object is.

exercises.question: Which two objects are made of METAL?
choices: a fork and a wooden chair
a rubber ball and a book
exercises.exp: A spoon and a nail are both made of metal — they are hard and shiny.

exercises.question: A brick wall FEELS rough. Which object also feels rough?
exercises.exp: Sandpaper has a rough surface used for sanding wood.

exercises.question: Which material is TRANSPARENT (lets all light through)?
exercises.exp: Clear glass is transparent — you can see right through it!

exercises.question: A plastic ruler is FLEXIBLE. What does flexible mean?
exercises.exp: Flexible means it can bend. A plastic ruler can bend a little.

exercises.question: Which property describes the COLOUR of an object?
exercises.exp: Colour is what we see — red, blue, green, and more!

exercises.question: Why is metal used to make pots and pans?
choices: it lets heat pass through easily
exercises.exp: Metal conducts heat well, so it is great for cooking.

exercises.question: Which object is made of MORE THAN ONE material?
exercises.exp: A pencil has wood, graphite (the lead), and a rubber eraser — three materials!

exercises.question: A sponge soaks up water easily. This is an example of which property?
exercises.exp: Absorbency describes how well a material soaks up liquid. Sponges are very absorbent!

exercises.question: Which material would be best for making a window?
exercises.exp: Clear glass is transparent so light passes through and you can see outside — perfect for windows!

exercises.question: A wool sweater keeps you warm. What property of wool makes it good for this?
choices: it is a good insulator that traps warm air
exercises.exp: Wool fibres trap warm air close to your body — making it an excellent insulator against cold weather.

exercises.question: Which of these materials is the SOFTEST?
exercises.exp: Cotton wool is very soft — you can squish it easily. Granite and steel are very hard.

exercises.question: A rubber ball BOUNCES. This property is called ___.
exercises.exp: Elasticity lets rubber bounce back to its shape after being squashed — that is why balls bounce!

exercises.question: Which material would you use to make a frying pan handle so it does NOT get hot?
exercises.exp: Plastic and wood are poor conductors of heat — the handle stays cool while the metal pan heats up.

exercises.question: You drop a glass cup and a plastic cup from the same height. Which is more likely to break?
exercises.exp: Glass is brittle — it shatters easily when hit. Plastic is tougher and usually bounces.

exercises.question: A kitchen counter is made of smooth stone. Why is smooth stone a good choice?
choices: it is easy to clean and very hard
exercises.exp: Smooth, hard stone counters are durable, easy to wipe clean, and resist scratches — ideal for kitchens!

exercises.question: Which property describes how well a material CONDUCTS electricity?
exercises.exp: Electrical conductivity tells us if electricity can flow through a material. Metals conduct electricity well.

exercises.question: A boat is made of WOOD. Which property of wood makes it useful for boats?
exercises.exp: Many types of wood are less dense than water, so they float — great for making boats and canoes!

exercises.question: Which material would make the BEST playground slide — fast and smooth?
exercises.exp: Smooth stainless steel has very little friction, so you slide down quickly and easily — perfect for slides!

exercises.question: A builder needs a material that is STRONG and can hold heavy loads. Which is best?
exercises.exp: Steel is extremely strong — it can hold enormous loads. Buildings and bridges use steel frames!

exercises.question: Which object is OPAQUE (you cannot see through it)?
exercises.exp: A wooden door is opaque — no light passes through it at all.

exercises.question: Ice is HARD and SOLID. When it melts to water, the material is still ___.
choices: the same material in a different state
exercises.exp: Ice and water are both H₂O — same material, different state. Melting is a physical change.

exercises.question: A raincoat needs to be WATERPROOF. Which material would NOT work?
exercises.exp: Tissue paper absorbs water instantly — it would be useless as a raincoat! You need waterproof materials.

exercises.question: Which property tells you a material can be pulled into thin wires?
exercises.exp: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires. Copper is very ductile — it is used in electrical wires!

exercises.question: A scientist wants to compare the HARDNESS of rocks. What could she do?
choices: try to scratch each rock with a nail — harder rocks resist scratching
look at the colour of each rock
exercises.exp: Hardness is tested by scratching — a harder material scratches a softer one. This is the Mohs scale idea!

exercises.question: Which material is both WATERPROOF and FLEXIBLE?
exercises.exp: Rubber is both waterproof and flexible — that is why it is used for wellington boots and garden hoses!

exercises.question: A material that LETS ELECTRICITY THROUGH is called a ___.
exercises.exp: Conductors let electricity flow through them. Most metals — copper, silver, gold — are excellent conductors.

exercises.question: Which word describes a material that does NOT let light pass through?
exercises.exp: Opaque materials block all light. A brick wall and a wooden door are opaque.

exercises.question: Frosted glass lets SOME light through but you cannot see clearly. It is ___.
exercises.exp: Translucent materials let some light pass through but scatter it. Frosted glass and tissue paper are translucent.

exercises.question: Which material is the BEST electrical insulator?
exercises.exp: Rubber does not conduct electricity — it is an insulator. That is why wire coatings are made of rubber or plastic.

exercises.question: A chair needs to be strong AND comfortable. Which pair of materials works best?
exercises.exp: Steel provides strength while foam provides comfort. Combining materials uses the best properties of each!

exercises.question: Which material would you use to keep a drink COLD for a long time?
exercises.exp: Foam insulation traps air and slows heat transfer — it keeps cold things cold and hot things hot!

exercises.question: You want to see through a container AND keep water inside. Which is best?
exercises.exp: Clear plastic is transparent AND waterproof — perfect for a container where you need to see the contents.

exercises.question: A magnetic material is attracted to a magnet. Which item is magnetic?
exercises.exp: Steel contains iron, which is magnetic. Wooden, glass, and plastic objects are not attracted to magnets.

exercises.question: Why do winter coats have a fluffy filling inside?
choices: to trap air and keep heat in — air is a good insulator
exercises.exp: Trapped air is an excellent insulator. Fluffy fillings trap tiny pockets of air that stop your body heat from escaping!

exercises.question: A material that can be stretched and returns to its original shape is ___.
exercises.exp: Elastic materials stretch and spring back. Rubber bands, lycra, and springs are all elastic.

exercises.question: Which property describes how easily a material BREAKS when bent?
exercises.exp: Brittle materials break easily when bent or hit. Glass and ceramic are brittle — they shatter rather than bend.

exercises.question: Cotton soaks up sweat from your skin. Which property makes cotton good for T-shirts?
exercises.exp: Cotton is very absorbent — it soaks up moisture from your skin and keeps you comfortable.

exercises.question: You need a material for a cutting board that is hard AND safe for food. Which is best?
exercises.exp: Hard plastic or wood cutting boards are tough enough to cut on and safe to use with food.

exercises.question: Which describes a material's THERMAL conductivity?
choices: how well it passes heat from hot to cold
exercises.exp: Thermal conductivity is how easily heat travels through a material. Metal pots are thermally conductive.

exercises.question: A material that returns to its original shape after squeezing is said to be ___.
exercises.exp: Elastic materials bounce back to their original shape. Foam, rubber, and sponges are all elastic materials.

exercises.question: Gold can be beaten into very thin sheets. This property is called ___.
exercises.exp: Malleability means a material can be hammered into thin sheets without breaking. Gold and copper are malleable.

exercises.question: Which material makes the BEST handle for a frying pan?
choices: plastic or wood — they are poor heat conductors (insulators)
exercises.exp: Pan handles should not conduct heat to your hand. Plastic and wood are poor heat conductors — ideal for handles!

exercises.question: You are building a model bridge. Which material best supports heavy loads without bending?
choices: thick balsa wood or stiff card
exercises.exp: For bridges, you need stiff, strong materials. Thick balsa wood or stiff card can support more load than thin paper.

exercises.question: A material described as POROUS has many tiny holes. Which is porous?
choices: a rock with many tiny spaces (like pumice)
exercises.exp: Pumice rock is very porous — it has so many holes that it actually floats on water! Sponges are also porous.

exercises.question: Recycling materials is important because it ___.
choices: reduces the need to extract new raw materials from the Earth
exercises.exp: Recycling saves energy and natural resources. Reusing materials like metal, glass, and plastic protects the Earth!
